# StrtokStateClobbered

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Detect starting a second two-argument strtok sequence between an initial sequence call and its one-argument continuation on the same reachable path.

## Example

```php{2}
<?php
$first=strtok($a,','); strtok($b,':'); $next=strtok(',');
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 2: Keep strtok sequences separate.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- Report starting a second two-argument strtok sequence between an initial sequence call and its one-argument continuation on the same reachable path.
- Resolve builtin calls and named arguments before checking the contract. Project-local callees are considered only when their bodies or immutable summaries establish the required facts. The default is enabled, with positive proof required.
- The path is searched backwards from the continuation over the statements that precede it in the same statement list. The newest start is the closest statement that is a two-argument strtok call, bare or as the assigned value; the initial start is the next such statement before it. Statements in between need not be adjacent to either call.
- D4. A statement crossed by the search must be unable to start a sequence: it contains no function, method or static call, object creation, include, eval, yield, closure or arrow function. Between the newest start and the continuation, one-argument strtok calls are also accepted, since they only advance the current sequence. Any other statement ends the search without a report.
- When the statement list is the body of a `while`, `foreach` or `for` loop, or the main branch of an `if`, the search continues with the statements before that construct, provided its header (the condition, the iterated expression, or the `for` initializers and conditions) satisfies D4. This covers the nested tokenizer shape, where an inner sequence is started and consumed inside the loop that continues the outer one. Other enclosing constructs (`else`/`elseif` branches, `do`, `switch`, `try`, function bodies) end the search.

## Exceptions (no report)

- Completion/restart of the same intended sequence, no later continuation, or a wrapper known not to invoke strtok are excluded. Two starts on the same string expression are a restart.
- Unresolved targets, incomplete required facts, suppressed findings and PHP versions lacking the referenced API or language feature produce no report. User declarations shadowing builtin names are not builtin contracts.
- The continuation belongs to the newest sequence: all three delimiter arguments are plain string literals, the continuation's delimiter equals the newest start's and differs from the initial start's. The initial call then only took a leading token (`$scheme = strtok($url, ':'); $name = strtok($file, '.'); $ext = strtok('.');`). When a delimiter is not a literal, or both starts share the delimiter, the owner is ambiguous and the report is kept.

## Fix

No automatic fix: independent tokenizer state requires restructuring.

## PHP versions

Apply only on PHP versions supporting the referenced APIs and syntax (within PHP 5.3–8.5). Builtin behavior and argument contracts follow the configured PHP version. Extension-specific calls require resolved extension API symbols; do not treat same-named application functions as extension calls.

## Options

None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "StrtokStateClobbered": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore StrtokStateClobbered
```
